en: Agreement or harmony; a formal treaty; to give or grant
hook: ACCORD: hearts (cor) in agreement.
story: Accord. Agreement or harmony; also, a formal treaty, or to grant something. For years, two neighbouring families quarrelled over a mango tree growing right on the wall between their homes. Every summer brought shouting about whose mangoes were whose. At last the elders sat down together and reached an accord: each family keeps the fruit on its own side, and the first basket of the season is shared. Now the families live in accord. Accord holds the Latin cor, heart: hearts brought together. So, what word means a peaceful agreement between two sides? ... Accord.

gre.s: After decades of hostility, the two neighboring states finally reached a historic ____ on sharing the river's waters, though skeptics doubted it would survive the next drought.
gre.clue: though skeptics doubted it would survive the next drought

example: Under the new accord, the two universities will let their students take courses at either campus without paying extra fees.

en: Harmful or unfavorable
hook: ADVERSE: like an ADVERSARY, working against you.
story: Adverse. Harmful or unfavourable. Kyle had saved for months to visit a coral island with his friends. The night before, the coast guard announced adverse weather: high winds and rough seas, with all ships cancelled. Standing at the jetty, watching grey waves crash, Kyle [sigh] let go of the trip. Adverse conditions had won, but everyone was safe. Adverse shares its root with adversary: adverse weather is your opponent. Do not confuse it with averse, which means unwilling. So, what word describes conditions that work against you? ... Adverse.

gre.s: The drug trial was halted early because several participants suffered ____ reactions, including severe rashes and dangerously high fevers.
gre.clue: including severe rashes and dangerously high fevers

example: Doctors warned that staying up past midnight before every exam can have adverse effects on both memory and mood.

en: Based on random choice or personal whim rather than reason
hook: ARBITRARY: like an ARBITER who decides by flipping a coin.
story: Arbitrary. Based on random choice or personal whim, not reason. Jenna's landlord in the city made new rules whenever he felt like it. One month he banned guests after nine. The next, he banned drying clothes on the roof. Then he raised the rent twice in one year, with no reason except his mood. Jenna and her flatmates never knew what tomorrow's rule would be. Every decision was arbitrary. The word comes from arbiter, a judge free to decide however he pleased. So, what word describes a rule made by whim rather than reason? ... Arbitrary.

gre.s: Employees resented the new promotion policy, which seemed entirely ____, rewarding some workers and passing over others for no discernible reason.
gre.clue: for no discernible reason

example: The border between the two provinces looks arbitrary on the map, a straight line drawn by colonial officials who never visited the region.

en: To regard something as caused by; a quality or feature
hook: ATTRIBUTE: give TRIBUTE (credit) to the cause.
story: Attribute. To regard something as caused by a particular thing; as a noun, a quality or feature. At ninety, Ella's grandmother still walks to the market every morning. When neighbours ask her secret, she [chuckle] holds up three fingers. She attributes her long life to a morning walk, a little rice, and never holding a grudge. Ella thinks her real attribute is her cheerfulness. Attribute and tribute share a Latin root meaning to assign or give: when you attribute something, you assign the credit to its cause. So, what verb means to credit an effect to a cause? ... Attribute.

gre.s: Although the coach was quick to ____ the team's victory to his new training regimen, most observers credited the opposing goalkeeper's uncharacteristic blunders.
gre.clue: most observers credited the opposing goalkeeper's uncharacteristic blunders

example: Doctors attribute this year's sharp rise in dengue cases to an unusually long and wet monsoon season.

en: Serving as an extra or backup source of help
hook: AUXILIARY: AUX cable, extra support.
story: Auxiliary. Serving as extra or backup help. Halfway through Sarah's wedding reception at a community centre, the power went out. The music stopped, the fans fell silent, and three hundred guests sat in the dark. [gasp] Sarah's father held his breath. Then, with a roar from the back of the building, the auxiliary generator came to life. The lights blazed, [laugh] and the guests cheered. Think of the aux cable in a car: aux is short for auxiliary, an extra input beside the main one. So, what word describes a backup source of help? ... Auxiliary.

gre.s: Although the main pump handles routine cooling, engineers installed ____ pumps that switch on automatically whenever demand exceeds its capacity.
gre.clue: whenever demand exceeds its capacity

example: When the main ferry broke down, the company sent two auxiliary boats so that passengers would not miss the Eid rush home.

en: Having enough skill or knowledge to do something successfully
hook: COMPETENT: able to COMPETE.
story: Competent. Having enough skill or knowledge to do something well. When the ceiling fan in Evan's flat began to spark, his father called a young electrician from the lane. He was not famous, and he arrived on a bicycle. But within twenty minutes he found the burnt wire, replaced it, tested every switch, and charged a fair price. The young man was competent. Competent means fully able, not necessarily brilliant; it shares a Latin root with compete, as if able to hold your own. So, what word describes someone with enough skill to do the job well? ... Competent.

gre.s: Although not brilliant, the new manager proved thoroughly ____, handling every crisis calmly and efficiently.
gre.clue: handling every crisis calmly and efficiently

example: Nasrin is a competent driver, but she still asks her brother to take the wheel on the busy Dhaka-Chattogram highway.

en: Believable enough to be trusted or taken seriously
hook: CREDIBLE: has CREDIT, so you can believe it.
story: Credible. Believable enough to be trusted. One evening, a message spread through Ashley's family group: a cyclone would hit the city that very night. Her aunt began packing bags in a panic. Ashley calmly checked the official bulletin from the Meteorological Department, which said the storm would stay far out at sea. That source was credible; the forwarded message was not. Her aunt [sigh] sat down and unpacked. Credible comes from the Latin for believe, like credit and credentials. So, what word describes a source you can trust? ... Credible.

gre.s: The jury found the witness's account ____, since it matched the physical evidence in every detail.
gre.clue: it matched the physical evidence in every detail

example: For a threat of punishment to work, a parent must make it credible, so empty warnings soon lose their effect.

en: To restrain or keep in check
hook: CURB: the street CURB keeps cars from going too far.
story: Curb. To restrain something or keep it in check. Paul used to drink six cups of tea a day, each with three spoons of sugar. After his doctor warned him about diabetes, his daughter Molly stuck a chart on the fridge. Each week, one spoon less. Paul grumbled, but slowly he curbed his sweet tooth. By winter, he took his tea with no sugar at all. Think of the curb at the side of a road: it stops cars from going too far, just as you curb a habit. So, what verb means to hold something back? ... Curb.

gre.s: Hoping to ____ the spread of the disease, health officials closed schools and banned large gatherings for a month, despite protests from businesses.
gre.clue: closed schools and banned large gatherings

example: The central bank raised interest rates to curb inflation, which had pushed the price of onions to a record high.

en: Done consciously and intentionally (adj.); to think carefully before deciding (verb)
hook: DELIBERATE: done with LIBERTY of choice, on purpose.
story: Deliberate. Done on purpose; as a verb, to think carefully before deciding. In the last over of a tense match, the young bowler Connor walked back slowly to his mark. He was deliberating: a fast ball, or a slow one? The crowd roared. Then he bowled a deliberate slower ball. The batsman swung far too early, and the stumps flew. Deliberate comes from the Latin libra, a pair of scales: to deliberate is to weigh your options carefully. So, what word describes an act done with clear intention? ... Deliberate.

gre.s: Investigators concluded that the fire was not an accident but a ____ act, pointing to traces of fuel poured near every exit.
gre.clue: pointing to traces of fuel poured near every exit

example: The professor's long pause before answering was deliberate, a way of making the students think harder about their own question.

en: To overshadow; to surpass or make less important
hook: ECLIPSE: like the moon blocking out the sun.
story: Eclipse. To overshadow; to surpass and make something seem less important. At every family gathering, Kayla always sang first, and everyone praised her. Then one holiday, her nine-year-old cousin Lily sang an old folk song in a voice so clear that the whole room fell silent. Kayla felt a sting, then a rush of pride. Her little cousin's talent had eclipsed her own. In a solar eclipse, the moon slides in front of the sun and hides its light; when one person eclipses another, they outshine them. So, what verb means to outshine and overshadow? ... Eclipse.

gre.s: Although the novelist was celebrated in her lifetime, her reputation came to ____ that of her more famous brother only after both had died.
gre.clue: her more famous brother

example: The huge success of her second album soon eclipsed her debut, which few listeners now remember.

en: Originating from a distant foreign country; strikingly unusual
hook: EXOTIC: EXternal, from the outside world.
story: Exotic. Coming from a distant foreign country; strikingly unusual. The first time Jason saw a dragon fruit in a city supermarket, he stopped and stared. Its skin was hot pink with green flames, and inside the white flesh was dotted with tiny black seeds. It looked truly exotic. Today, farmers across the country grow dragon fruit, and it is sold from carts beside the road. Exotic comes from the Greek exo, meaning outside: something exotic comes from the outside world. So, what word describes something strikingly unusual, from far away? ... Exotic.

gre.s: The botanist travelled to remote islands in search of ____ plants that had never been described in any European catalogue.
gre.clue: had never been described in any European catalogue

example: Pet shops in Katabon sell exotic birds from Africa and South America, though some of them are smuggled into the country illegally.

en: To prevent something from succeeding; a person who contrasts with another
hook: FOIL: wrap the plan in FOIL so it can't work.
story: Foil. To stop a plan from succeeding; also, a person who contrasts with another. Brooke's friends spent a week planning a surprise party for her birthday. The balloons were up, the cake was hidden, and everyone was crouched behind the sofa. Then her six-year-old nephew ran to the door and shouted, "Come quickly, everyone is hiding!" [laugh] One sentence foiled the whole plan. Picture a plan wrapped up in foil so it cannot breathe. A foil is also a character whose contrast makes another shine. So, what verb means to stop a plan from working? ... Foil.

gre.s: An alert bank clerk managed to ____ the robbery by quietly pressing a silent alarm, and the police arrived before the gang could reach the vault.
gre.clue: by quietly pressing a silent alarm

example: A sudden thunderstorm foiled the climbers' plan to reach the summit before noon, forcing them back to the lower camp.

en: The outer edge; unconventional or extreme views outside the mainstream
hook: FRINGE: the edge of a scarf, far from the center.
story: Fringe. The outer edge; also, views far outside the mainstream. At a corner diner, Caleb's uncle insists every evening that the moon landing was faked. The other men sip their tea, roll their eyes, and talk about cricket instead. Caleb knows his uncle is a kind man, but his ideas sit on the fringe, believed by very few. Picture the fringe of a scarf, those loose threads hanging at the far edge, far from the centre of the cloth. So, what word describes views far from the mainstream? ... Fringe.

gre.s: Once dismissed as a ____ theory held by only a handful of eccentrics, the idea has since gained wide acceptance among mainstream scientists.
gre.clue: held by only a handful of eccentrics

example: The party began as a fringe movement meeting in a single tea shop, yet within a decade it had won seats in parliament.

en: Having a tendency or willingness to do something
hook: INCLINED: LEANING toward something, like an inclined plane.
story: Inclined. Having a tendency or willingness to do something. On cold January mornings up north, Zoe is never inclined to leave her heavy quilt. The fog presses on the windows, and the floor feels like ice. [sigh] But one morning, the smell of steamed rice cakes and date molasses drifted in from the kitchen. Suddenly she felt very inclined to get up, and she [laugh] ran out in her socks. Think of an inclined road that leans in one direction: an inclined person leans toward doing something. So, what word means leaning toward doing something? ... Inclined.

gre.s: Having been burned by investments before, she was not ____ to trust the salesman's promises of guaranteed returns.
gre.clue: Having been burned by investments before

example: After the long train ride, few of the tourists were inclined to climb the hundred steps up to the old temple.

en: Showing a lack of experience, wisdom, or judgment
hook: NAIVE: like a NATIVE newcomer who doesn't know the city's tricks.
story: Naive. Showing a lack of experience or judgment. Hailey saw a new smartphone advertised on a Facebook page for half its usual price. The seller wanted full payment in advance, and he sounded so friendly. She sent the money. A week later, the parcel arrived, and inside was a single bar of soap. Her elder brother did not scold her. He just said she had been naive. Naive and native come from the same Latin root meaning born: a naive person is as unworldly as a newborn. So, what word describes someone too trusting because of inexperience? ... Naive.

gre.s: Only a ____ observer would take the company's promises at face value, since it has broken nearly every pledge it has made in the past decade.
gre.clue: since it has broken nearly every pledge it has made in the past decade

example: It was naive of the startup founders to assume that investors would fund them without first seeing any sales figures.

en: Not well known or hard to understand (adj.); to hide or make unclear (verb)
hook: OBSCURE: hidden in the dark (obscurity).
story: Obscure. Not well known, or hard to understand; as a verb, to hide or make unclear. Browsing the second-hand bookstalls downtown, Eli found a thin poetry book with a cracked spine. Dust and water stains had obscured the poet's name. He had never heard of her, and neither had the seller. But that night the poems made him cry. He promised himself he would find out who this obscure poet was. Obscure comes from the Latin for dark: something obscure stays in the shadows. So, what word describes a writer almost nobody knows? ... Obscure.

gre.s: Once an ____ figure known only to a few specialists, the painter is now celebrated in major museums around the world.
gre.clue: known only to a few specialists

example: The prizewinning novel first appeared from an obscure press in Rajshahi that had never sold more than a few hundred copies of any title.

en: Very great or intense; having deep insight
hook: PROFOUND: as deep as the ocean FOUNDATION.
story: Profound. Very great or intense; also, showing deep insight. When Mason failed his first university exam, he went home to his village, ashamed. His grandfather took him down to the river at sunset. "Look," he said. "The river never runs straight, yet it always reaches the sea." Mason stood silent for a long time. Those simple words had a profound effect on him. Profound shares a Latin root with foundation, from the word for bottom: a profound idea reaches deep down. So, what word describes words of deep insight? ... Profound.

gre.s: Although the lecture was delivered in simple language, its insights were ____, forcing listeners to reconsider assumptions they had held all their lives.
gre.clue: forcing listeners to reconsider assumptions they had held all their lives

example: The simple question of why the night sky is dark turned out to have profound implications for our picture of the universe.

en: To cause to become; to provide or give
hook: RENDER: RENDERS it into a new state.
story: Render. To cause someone or something to become; also, to give or provide. Julia opened the email in her dorm room and read the first line three times. A full scholarship. [gasp] She tried to call her mother, but the news had rendered her speechless, and she could only laugh and cry into the phone. Her mother understood anyway. Render comes from a Latin word meaning to give back: a doctor renders help, and news can render you speechless, giving you back in a new state. So, what verb means to cause someone to become something? ... Render.

gre.s: Throughout the crisis, volunteers continued to ____ assistance to stranded travelers, offering food, shelter, and free rides to the nearest town.
gre.clue: offering food, shelter, and free rides to the nearest town

example: Local fishermen rendered vital help to the coast guard, guiding rescue boats through channels that did not appear on any chart.

en: Shy and quiet, preferring to stay out of sight
hook: GRE trick: RETIRING means shy — she RETIRES to her room when guests come.
story: Retiring. Shy and quiet, preferring to stay out of sight. At every family wedding, while cousins danced and aunts gossiped, Claire slipped quietly up to the rooftop with a cup of tea. Relatives called her the quiet one. Then one winter, her paintings of mangrove forests filled a city gallery, and the family learned what she had been doing all those years. Their retiring Claire had a voice after all. A retiring person retires from the crowd, the way a worker retires from the office. So, what word describes someone shy who keeps out of the spotlight? ... Retiring.

gre.s: Though her paintings were bold and flamboyant, the artist herself was ____, avoiding interviews and rarely appearing even at her own exhibitions.
gre.clue: avoiding interviews and rarely appearing even at her own exhibitions

example: The retiring mathematician declined every invitation to speak about her famous proof and went on quietly teaching first-year calculus.

en: The art of persuasive speaking or writing; sometimes, language that is impressive but insincere
hook: RHETORIC: a RHETORICAL question doesn't need an answer — it's just for effect.
story: Rhetoric. The art of persuasive speaking; also, language that sounds impressive but is insincere. Before a local election, a candidate's microphone boomed through Derek's small town. Smooth new roads, a modern hospital, a job for every young person. Crowds clapped and garlands piled up. Five years later, the main road still flooded every monsoon, and Derek's mother still travelled two hours to see a doctor. It had all been rhetoric. A rhetor was a public speaker in ancient Greece, and a rhetorical question is asked only for effect. So, what word means fine speech without real substance? ... Rhetoric.

gre.s: Voters had grown weary of the candidate's ____, noting that years of grand speeches had produced not a single new road or school.
gre.clue: years of grand speeches had produced not a single new road or school

example: Behind the minister's rhetoric about a digital revolution, most village schools still had no computers and no reliable electricity.

en: Strong, sturdy, and healthy; vigorous
hook: ROBUST: like a ROBOT, strong and hard to break.
story: Robust. Strong, sturdy and healthy. Ian's grandfather is seventy-eight, yet every morning he walks to his rice field, carries sacks on his shoulder, and swims in the pond before lunch. When Ian, at twenty, grew tired halfway through the field, the old man [chuckle] took the sack from him. "City boy," he said fondly. Ian was amazed at how robust he still was. Robust comes from the Latin robur, meaning oak: a robust person stands as firm as an oak tree. So, what word describes someone strong, sturdy and full of health? ... Robust.

gre.s: Far from being fragile, the economy proved surprisingly ____, recovering within months from a shock that analysts had expected to last years.
gre.clue: Far from being fragile

example: Bamboo scaffolding is surprisingly robust, and Dhaka builders still use it to put up apartment towers many storeys high.

en: To go around the edge of; to avoid dealing with an issue
hook: GRE trick: to SKIRT means to go around the edge, like a skirt's hem.
story: Skirt. To go around the edge of something; also, to avoid dealing with an issue. At a family dinner, Madison's aunt leaned over and asked, for the fifth time that year, when she planned to marry. Madison smiled and said, "Auntie, your mango pickle is amazing. How do you make it?" Her aunt [chuckle] began explaining at once. Madison had skirted the question again. A skirt runs around the edge, and when you skirt an issue, you go around it without ever going through it. So, what verb means to dodge a topic? ... Skirt.

gre.s: Rather than addressing the scandal directly, the spokesperson tried to ____ the issue by talking at length about the company's charitable work.
gre.clue: Rather than addressing the scandal directly

example: The new history textbook skirts the controversy over the war's causes, offering a list of dates instead of an explanation.

en: Serious and sensible; not drunk
hook: GRE trick: SOBER means serious and realistic, not just alcohol-free.
story: Sober. Serious, sensible and realistic; also, not drunk. Ethan and his friends were thrilled about their idea for a food delivery business. They talked of millions of customers and new branches in every city. Then his elder sister, an accountant, read their plan. She did not mock them. She gave a sober view: costs, risks, and how long profit might take. The boys went quiet, then started again, more carefully. A sober person is not drunk, and a sober judgement is not drunk on excitement either. So, what word describes a calm, realistic assessment? ... Sober.

gre.s: After years of wildly optimistic forecasts, the committee's latest report offered a more ____ assessment, acknowledging that the economy might not recover for a decade.
gre.clue: acknowledging that the economy might not recover for a decade

example: A sober look at the club's finances showed that it could not afford a foreign coach for at least two more seasons.

en: Serious, strict, and unyielding
hook: STERN: like the STERN (back) of a ship, firm and unmoving.
story: Stern. Serious, strict and unyielding. Every student at Rosa's school feared the headmaster. He never smiled in the corridor, and one stern look could silence a whole classroom. But when Rosa's father lost his job, it was this stern man who quietly paid her school fees for two years and told nobody. Rosa learned it only on her last day. Picture a stern captain standing at the stern of his ship, unmoving while the waves crash. So, what word describes someone serious and strict, who rarely smiles? ... Stern.

gre.s: Behind the judge's ____ exterior, which intimidated many lawyers, lay a deeply compassionate person.
gre.clue: which intimidated many lawyers

example: The referee gave the captain a stern warning, and for the rest of the match nobody dared to argue with a single decision.

en: Shaped by one's own feelings and tastes, not by facts
hook: SUBJECTIVE: depends on the SUBJECT, the person judging.
story: Subjective. Shaped by personal feelings and tastes, not by facts. Joe from the old city and Rita from the port town have argued for years about the best beef dish. Joe swears by the slow-cooked biryani from his neighbourhood. Rita says nothing beats the spicy beef feast of her home town. At their own wedding, they served both, [laugh] and the guests still argued. The question will never be settled, because taste is subjective. Subjective depends on the subject, the person judging; objective depends on the object itself. So, what word describes a judgement that depends on personal taste? ... Subjective.

gre.s: Because judges' scores in the competition are inevitably ____, organizers introduced a panel of five to reduce the influence of any one person's taste.
gre.clue: reduce the influence of any one person's taste

example: Pain is partly subjective, so two patients with the same injury may describe it in very different ways.

en: To make something milder or less extreme
hook: GRE trick: to TEMPER is to TONE DOWN, like tempering spicy food with yogurt.
story: Temper. To make something milder or less extreme. When Ryan found a fresh dent in his new motorbike, he was furious with his younger brother and began shouting. Their mother stepped between them. She reminded Ryan, gently, of the time he had crashed their father's bicycle into a pond. Ryan went quiet, then almost smiled. Her words had tempered his anger. Temper shares its root with temperate and temperature: to temper something is to bring it to a moderate heat. So, what verb means to soften or tone something down? ... Temper.

gre.s: Hoping to ____ the committee's harsh conclusions, the chair added a paragraph acknowledging the team's genuine achievements under difficult conditions.
gre.clue: acknowledging the team's genuine achievements

example: Grandfather tempered his strict rules with generous helpings of sweets, so the children never stayed angry with him for long.

en: Complete with regard to every detail
hook: THOROUGH: goes THROUGH everything.
story: Thorough. Complete, with attention to every detail. The week before the holiday, Anna's mother cleans the whole house. She wipes every fan blade, scrubs behind every cupboard, washes the curtains, and even dusts the tops of the door frames. Anna once tried to hide a little dust under a rug. Her mother lifted the rug at once. Nothing escapes such a thorough cleaning. Thorough was once simply a spelling of through: a thorough person goes through everything. So, what word describes work complete in every detail? ... Thorough.

gre.s: Unlike the hasty earlier investigation, the new inquiry was ____, interviewing every witness and examining every document.
gre.clue: interviewing every witness and examining every document

example: Before buying the secondhand car, Imtiaz asked a mechanic to do a thorough check of the brakes, engine, and wiring.

en: Done for appearance only; a symbol or sign
hook: TOKEN: just a symbolic gesture, like a TOKEN coin.
story: Token. Done only for appearance; also, a symbol or sign. Every year, as the river ate away more of their village, families begged for a proper embankment. One morning, an official arrived with photographers, planted a single sapling on the riverbank, smiled for the cameras, and drove away. No embankment came. Even the sapling was soon washed away. It had been a token gesture. A token coin stands in for real money, and a token gesture stands in for real action. So, what word describes an action done only for show? ... Token.

gre.s: The government's ____ efforts at reform, which changed a few official titles but left the corrupt system entirely untouched, fooled no one.
gre.clue: changed a few official titles but left the corrupt system entirely untouched

example: The landlord made a token repair, painting over the damp patch on the wall without fixing the leaking pipe behind it.

en: Never done or known before
hook: UN-PRECEDENT-ED: no PRECEDENT, never happened before.
story: Unprecedented. Never done or known before. For generations, Vanessa's family crossed the mighty river by ferry, often waiting for hours at the landing in heat or fog. In June twenty twenty-two, the great bridge opened, and her father drove to the capital without a ferry for the first time in his life. He kept saying it was unprecedented. A precedent is an earlier example to follow; something unprecedented has no earlier example at all. So, what word describes an event that has never happened before? ... Unprecedented.

gre.s: The flood was truly ____: in two hundred years of written records, the river had never risen even half as high.
gre.clue: had never risen even half as high

example: The team's run of fourteen straight victories was unprecedented in the league's sixty-year history.

en: Practical and able to succeed; workable
hook: VIABLE: has VITALITY, can survive.
story: Viable. Practical and able to succeed; workable. In the low southern wetlands, fields stay under water for months each year. So farmers there weave water hyacinth into thick floating beds, cover them with mud, and plant vegetables on top. When the water rises, the garden simply rises with it. Visitors are often surprised that a floating garden is a viable way to farm. Viable comes from the French vie, meaning life: a viable plan can live and survive. So, what word describes a plan that can actually work? ... Viable.

gre.s: Although solar power was once dismissed as too expensive, falling costs have made it a ____ alternative to coal in many countries.
gre.clue: falling costs have made it

example: Floating schools built on boats have proved a viable option for children in villages that monsoon floods cut off for months.
